The Highland Scenic Loop: 5 Days of Scotland's Best

This five-day motorcycle circuit from Inverness takes in the most dramatic landscapes in the Scottish Highlands — Glencoe's towering mountains, the wild Torridon peninsula, the Bealach na Bà, and the Great Glen. It's Scotland's greatest hits in a manageable, unforgettable loop.

Day 1: Inverness to Glencoe (110 miles)

Head south on the A82 along the shores of Loch Ness and through Fort Augustus. Continue south through the Great Glen to Fort William, then into Glencoe — Britain's most dramatic glen. The ride through Glencoe itself is the highlight of the day and possibly the tour.

  • Key stops: Urquhart Castle (Loch Ness), Fort Augustus canal locks, Glencoe Visitor Centre
  • Accommodation: Glencoe village or Ballachulish

Day 2: Glencoe to Torridon (130 miles)

Head north via Fort William and the A830 Road to the Isles towards Mallaig. Turn north through Glenfinnan (the viaduct!) and continue via Invergarry and Glen Shiel to Torridon. The single-track roads around Torridon are among the most spectacular in Scotland.

  • Key stops: Glenfinnan Viaduct viewpoint, Eilean Donan Castle, Glen Shiel
  • Accommodation: Torridon village or Shieldaig

Day 3: Torridon and Applecross (80 miles)

A shorter day to savour the scenery. Ride the Bealach na Bà to Applecross, then take the coastal road back north to Torridon. This day contains the most dramatic riding of the tour — the Bealach na Bà is Britain's closest thing to an Alpine pass.

  • Key stops: Bealach na Bà summit viewpoint, Applecross Bay, Applecross Inn for seafood
  • Accommodation: Applecross or return to Torridon

Day 4: Torridon to Ullapool (90 miles)

Head north through Kinlochewe and along Loch Maree — possibly the most beautiful loch in Scotland. Continue north through the dramatic Assynt landscape to Ullapool, a charming fishing town on Loch Broom.

  • Key stops: Loch Maree viewpoints, Inverewe Garden, Knockan Crag geological trail
  • Accommodation: Ullapool

Day 5: Ullapool to Inverness (60 miles)

A short final day through the eastern Highlands back to Inverness. The A835 through the Corrieshalloch Gorge and then east through Garve provides pleasant, flowing riding to close the tour. Read our Glencoe and Fort William Motorcycle Guide: Scotland's Dramatic Heart guide for more.

  • Key stops: Corrieshalloch Gorge and Falls of Measach, Rogie Falls (salmon leaping)
This loop covers approximately 470 miles in five days — an average of under 100 miles per day. This relaxed pace is deliberate. The Highlands reward slow exploration, not fast mileage. Linger at viewpoints, explore side roads, and let the landscape soak in.

Practical Notes

  • Fuel: Fill up at Fort William, Torridon/Kinlochewe area, and Ullapool. Don't let your tank drop below half in this region.
  • Accommodation: Book in advance for July/August. Shoulder season (May-June, September) offers better availability and often better weather.
  • Mobile signal: Very limited throughout. Download offline maps before departure.
  • Midges: June to September. Carry Smidge repellent and a head net.
keyTakeaways: This five-day circuit from Inverness covers about 470 miles at under 100 miles a day, taking in Glencoe, Torridon, Applecross and the Great Glen.
Day 3 delivers the Bealach na Ba to Applecross, Britain's closest thing to an Alpine pass.
Loch Maree on Day 4 is possibly the most beautiful loch in Scotland, on the way to Ullapool.
Fuel is sparse; fill up at Fort William, Torridon or Kinlochewe, and Ullapool, and never drop below half a tank.
Mobile signal is very limited throughout, so download offline maps before you leave.

faq.q: How many days should I allow for this loop?
faq.a: The loop is designed for five days, covering about 470 miles at an average of under 100 miles a day. This relaxed pace is deliberate: the Highlands reward slow exploration rather than fast mileage. Allowing five days lets you linger at viewpoints, explore side roads and cope with the changeable weather without feeling rushed on the single-track sections.

faq.q: Where can I refuel on the route?
faq.a: Fuel is sparse in the northwest Highlands. Fill up at Fort William, in the Torridon or Kinlochewe area, and at Ullapool. Do not let your tank drop below half in this region, as stations are widely spaced and some keep short hours. Planning refuelling stops around these towns removes the main logistical worry of touring the remote northwest.

faq.q: Is the Bealach na Ba suitable for a large touring bike?
faq.a: The Bealach na Ba is a steep single-track pass with tight hairpins, rising to Britain's most Alpine feel. Large touring bikes can ride it, but you must be comfortable with hill starts on steep gradients, blind bends and using passing places. In summer expect campervans and tourist traffic. Ride it early in the day and take Day 3 slowly to enjoy it.

faq.q: When is the best time of year to ride the loop?
faq.a: Shoulder season, May to June and September, offers the best combination of availability, quieter roads and often better weather. July and August are busiest and accommodation must be booked well ahead. Midges are active June to September, so carry Smidge repellent and a head net. Mobile signal is very limited throughout, so download offline maps before departure.
